Claire — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming us-west. Attaching the provisioning checklist below (inline) so your netops can start prepping:

--- Provisioning checklist (summary) ---
1) Cloud account & region: confirm account id (we need a cross-account role or peering info).
2) VPC/subnet ranges & NAT: send CIDR blocks and any reserved ranges.
3) Allowed egress: list of domains/IPs (we provide a short allowlist).
4) Expected QPS and concurrency for pilot (use 95th percentile): example: 200 rps peak, avg 60 rps.
5) Model footprint: typical token lengths & estimated prompt/response sizes (tokens).
6) Persistence & KV caches: will you need pinned KV caches per model instance?
7) SLA gates & scaling: target P99 latency and acceptable cold-start windows.
8) Procurement/PO ETA and billing contact.

Autoscale/burst policy proposal (initial):
- Pilot: start with 1 dedicated pool of 8xA100-equivalent GPUs in us-west with autoscale floor = 4 GPUs and ceiling = 16 GPUs; burst enabled to shared warm pool up to +8 GPUs when utilization > 85% for >5m.
- Warm-burst semantics: burst capacity is transient and best-effort — we’ll include fallback to a smaller generative model variant if burst unavailable.
- Observable signals: token/sec, queue length, instance utilization. We’ll surface costs per-minute by route in the console for transparency.

I’ll bring a short deck to the intake to walk through the checklist and the autoscale knobs.

Ben Carter
Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
